summary: The root "Aff" primarily denotes a sound or expression of disgust, impatience, or contempt, often made by blowing or exhaling. It signifies a strong dislike or disapproval, as in saying "Uff!

provenance.lane: Edward William Lane, An Arabic-English Lexicon (1863-93), public domain. Digital text via Perseus, Tufts University, CC BY-SA 3.0 US.
provenance.summary: Editorial summary derived from the Lane entry. NOT Lane's own wording. Shown as a gloss only; the Lane text below is the source.

headwords.def: أَفَّ, aor. يَؤُفٌّ (IDrd, M, Mgh, K,) and يَئِفُّ, (IDrd, M, K,) the latter agreeable with analogy, (TA,) [but the former, though irregular, is the more common,] inf. n. أَفٌّ; (M, Mgh;) and, inf. n. تأْفِيفٌ; (S, Mgh, K;) and; (M, K;) He said أُفِّ [q.
اَفَّفَ see 1, in three places.
تَاَفَّفَ see 2, in four places.
أَفْ and أَفِّ and أَفٍّ, or أَفٍ: see أُفٌّ.
إِفْ أف إف اف وفى and its vars. (differing only in having the ف movent): see the next paragraph.

أُفٌّ Dirt, or filth; as also: (S:) you say, أُفَّا لَهُ, and, Dirt, or filth, to him; in which the tenween is for the purpose of rendering them indeterminate; (S;) and أُفَّ لَهُ وَ تُفٌّ; (T;) and وَتُفَّةً; and أُفَّا وَتُفَّا; (T, S;) the latter of which is an imitative sequent: (S:) or أُفٌّ signifies the dirt of the ear; and تُفٌّ, the dirt of the nails; (As, T, M, K; but in the last, of the nail; ) the phrases mentioned above being used on the occasion of deeming a thing dirty or filthy,…
أَفَّةٌ: see إِفَّانٌ, in two places.

أُفَّةٌ: see أُفٌّ, in four places. Also A dirty, a filthy, an unclean, man: (K:) from أُفٌّ signifying the “dirt of the nail.” (TA.) One in want; poor; possessing little: (K:) from أَفَفٌ signifying “a thing little in quantity.” (TA.) A coward: (K:) as though originally ُو أُفَّةٍ, i. e. holding back, by reason of disgust, ( مُتَأَفِّفٌ,) from fight: (TA:) or experiencing vexation or disgust, and languid or sluggish, in war: (IAar:) also heavy, or sluggish. (IAth.)
إِفَّةٌ أفه افه افة فاه وفى آفة: see إِفَّانٌ in three places.
أَفَفٌ Vexation, distress of mind, or disgust. (T, IAth, K.) See also أُفٌّ, in three places. And see إِفَّانٌ, in three places.
أَفَهْ and أَفَّهٌ and أٌفَّهٌ and أُفِّهْ and أُفُّهْ: see أُفٌّ.
أُفَّى, pronounced in three different ways; and
إِفَّا افا: and إِفَّى and إِفِّى: see أُفٌّ.
أُفُوفَةٌ: see what next follows.

أَفَّافٌ A man who says أُفِّ much or often; (M, TA;) as also, accord. to the copies of the O and TS and K; but in other lexicons: in the O, one who ceases not to say to another أُفِّ لَكَ: in the Jm, the last of these three words is explained as meaning one who ceases no to say this at some of his affairs. (TA.)

إِفَّانٌ أفين إفان إيفان افان (T, S, M, K) and أَفَّانٌ (T, TS, L, K) and (S, M, K) and (T, L, K) and (L, M) and (M) and, (T, M, S, K, &c.,) of the measure تَفْعِلَةٌ, [being originally تَأْفِفَةٌ,] accord. to J, who appears to be right in saying so, (IB,) and so accord.
آفِ آف and آفِّ and آفٍ and آفٍّ: see أُفٌّ.
أُوفُوفَةٌ: see أَفَّافٌ.
تَئِفَّةٌ: see إِفّانٌ, in three places.
مُتَأَفِّفٌ عَنِ القِتَالِ [app. Holding back, by reason of disgust, from fight; as though saying أُفّ at the mention thereof: see أُفَّةٌ ]. (TA.)

headword_note: Lane indexes geminate roots with two letters where the Corpus uses three; both spellings are resolved here.
